headline: Sensex ends flat above 81,900 while Nifty holds 25,200 level; Smallcaps outperform

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Foreign institutional investor (FII) inflows provided support to market sentiment.
Lower crude oil prices helped lift market trading in early sessions.
Banking stocks led an early trade rebound across benchmark indices.
Retail inflation crossed the RBI upper limit to reach 6.1% in October 2026.
whatHappening: Sensex closed above 81,900 while NIFTY50 ended around the 25,229 level.
Oil India reported a 53% surge in Q2 net profit to ₹2,521 crore on higher realization.
Ola Electric narrowed its Q2 net loss to ₹362 crore despite a 39% revenue decline.
Roto Pumps surged 14% while Nifty Smallcap 100 outperformed for a second consecutive session.
summary: Indian equity markets closed flat to higher on November 12, with Sensex remaining above 81,900 and Nifty holding 25,200. Gains were driven by strong FII inflows, lower crude oil prices, and buying in banking and smallcap stocks. Meanwhile, macro concerns emerged as domestic retail inflation surged to 6.1% in October, exceeding the RBI's upper tolerance threshold.
